passage:
Helen had an orange notebook. She carried it everywhere and wrote down words she did not know. Some words came from books. Others came from signs, songs, or conversations.
Her friends thought it was too much work. They said phones could translate words more quickly.
Helen agreed, but she liked writing words by hand. She also wrote example sentences. Once, she learned the word "patient" from a hospital sign. Later, she wrote, "My brother is not patient when the computer is slow."
By the end of the year, the notebook was full. Helen did not remember every word, but she remembered many stories behind them.
A phone can give an answer quickly. A notebook can help a word stay longer.
